name: Tal Roded
problem_details: Community board meeting records exist as unstructured PDFs with no keyword search, no cross-board comparability, and no linkage to agency data. Even tech-forward CBs using Airtable cannot do universal keyword search across meetings. He is building Block Party, an AI-powered knowledge base covering all 59 NYC CBs.

name: Nathan Storey
organization: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation
problem_details: AI assistants cannot reliably query government open data because no standard interface exists across the 559 Socrata portals used by US governments. He is building an MCP server layer to fix this but needs government adoption partners. He also ran a vTaiwan-inspired participatory design process at NYC DHS with 300+ frontline staff.

name: Sebastian Hallum Clarke
problem_details: NYC property tax rules produce wildly different effective rates for similar properties, but no public tool makes this legible. He built an interactive property tax map from public data because no government tool existed.

name: Daniel Golliher
problem_details: No institution teaches people going into government how that government actually works -- its legal structure, budget cycle, legislative drafting, or procurement constraints. People learn on the job years late. Maximum New York is teaching 180+ students but cannot scale without curriculum partners.

name: Mark Headd
problem_details: When agencies modernize legacy systems they migrate code but lose institutional knowledge of how the system was supposed to work. He built SpecOps -- a spec-driven modernization approach -- because this knowledge destruction repeats endlessly. The federal ATO compliance process is a second blocker, adding months of delay before agencies can ship anything.

name: Waldo Jaquith
problem_details: Government software projects succeed 13% of the time because capital funding models force single massive fixed-price contracts, which guarantee failure. The IV&V oversight process compounds this by evaluating compliance with requirements rather than whether software works.

name: Evagelia Emily Tavoulareas
problem_details: Policy schools train people in what to do, not how to deliver it, producing a structural gap between policy design and technology implementation. Policymakers need to be conversant in technology -- able to manage environments where delivery people can succeed. Current curricula miss this entirely.

name: Merici Vinton
problem_details: Government digital services that demonstrably work -- Direct File had an NPS that beat Apple -- get killed for political reasons with no institutional mechanism to protect them. The knowledge of how to build them walks out with the people who leave.
help_source: Just want it on the record

name: Rebecca Heywood
problem_details: The civic tech talent pipeline has no legible on-ramp. People with transferable skills from tech, design, and data cannot distinguish a forward-thinking government digital team from a legacy IT shop. The landscape is invisible from the outside.

name: Santi Ruiz
problem_details: Tacit knowledge of how government gets things done is locked in practitioners' heads. Even people inside government do not know what authorities they have -- Other Transaction Authority is a legal procurement flexibility most agencies have but do not use because nobody told them.

name: Don Moynihan
organization: University of Michigan / Better Government Lab
problem_details: Administrative burden is a designed outcome, not random friction. Government programs deny benefits to eligible people because of complexity: 212-question applications, browser-specific systems, and verification steps requiring documents most people do not have.

name: Brendan Babb
problem_details: Small and mid-size cities have the same infrastructure monitoring needs as large ones -- potholes, unplowed roads, damaged assets -- but cannot afford data science teams. No off-the-shelf tool makes AI-powered asset monitoring accessible to a 290k-person city with a small IT department.

name: 17A
problem_details: States implementing Medicaid work requirements and SNAP eligibility reviews under H.R. 1 lack decision frameworks, technology guidance, and implementation toolkits for preserving coverage while meeting new federal requirements.

name: Nava PBC
problem_details: No open-source, state-adaptable technology exists for implementing Medicaid community engagement requirements under H.R. 1. Each state is building independently, guaranteeing coverage losses and duplicated cost. Nava is building shared tooling and seeking state partners.

name: Public Benefit Innovation Fund
problem_details: States administering SNAP and Medicaid cannot streamline applications, verify income efficiently, or communicate clearly with beneficiaries -- all at once, with limited staff and aging systems. Spring 2026 open call, $500k-$2M per award, $5M total pool.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center -- Digital Benefits Network
problem_details: Digital identity requirements for benefits programs (SNAP, WIC, TANF, Medicaid, UI) vary so widely across states that eligible residents are systematically locked out. No shared infrastructure or standards exist. Beeck published the dataset and is seeking partners to address the gaps.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center -- Digital Government Hub
problem_details: Practitioners working on government digital services have no single searchable library of field-relevant research, tools, and case studies. The Digital Government Hub is an attempt to fill this gap, currently organized around H.R. 1 implementation, benefits access, and UI modernization.

name: Federation of American Scientists
problem_details: Federal R&D investment is siloed across agencies with no coordination mechanism -- adjacent programs duplicate work and miss synthesis. FAS is actively seeking practitioner-authored policy memos with specific, actionable proposals. Current priority: AI fairness harms with concrete policy solutions.

name: Stanford RegLab
problem_details: 60-75% of Clean Water Act facilities self-reported noncompliance, but EPA lacks data-driven compliance monitoring. RegLab is building remote sensing tools and seeking agency partners. Second problem: IRS audit selection is racially biased -- Black taxpayers are 3-5x more likely to be audited -- and RegLab needs IRS partnership to test a fairer ML-based approach.

name: Alex Jutca
organization: Allegheny County Department of Human Services
problem_details: Child welfare agencies receive ~15,000 maltreatment referrals per year with no reliable way to decide which to investigate. Allegheny County built the AFST machine learning tool to help but most counties have nothing comparable. Separately, 1 in 5 parents in child welfare has an opioid use disorder -- a revolving door across incarceration, treatment, and relapse that no single system addresses.

name: Stephanie Pollack
problem_details: US transit projects fail because permitting is sequential rather than concurrent -- planning, environmental review, public engagement, and permits happen one after another with no reason they could not overlap. Post-COVID construction cost inflation up to 2% per month means every 5-month delay adds 10% to project cost, locking agencies into a compounding funding gap.

name: David Lebryk
problem_details: Government payment systems contain the data to detect fraud at scale, but it is siloed. When Treasury built cross-agency data matching between Labor, HHS, and Fiscal Service, fraud prevention jumped from $652M to $7.2B in one year. The program identified another $30B from 19 additional datasets. Systemic cross-agency data sharing remains the exception, not the infrastructure.

name: Judge Glock
problem_details: The federal civil service has not updated its HR systems since 1978 while states like Texas, Georgia, and Arizona have enacted broadly positive at-will employment and broadbanded pay reforms. Firing underperforming federal employees requires choosing between two broken statutory processes, neither of which yields accountability.

name: Sean Eke
problem_details: NYC City Council hearing transcripts are only accessible as video or unstructured PDFs -- no searchable, summarized, cross-linked record exists of what was said, by whom, or how it connects to legislation. He built Hearing Hearings, an AI tool summarizing hearings from YouTube transcripts and Legistar data, because no government system provides this.

name: Kate Green
problem_details: A decade of institutional knowledge on how to build high-performing government digital services -- accumulated at USDS, 18F, and agency digital teams -- is being lost as practitioners are pushed out, with no systematic mechanism to preserve or transmit it.
help_source: Just want it on the record

name: Jen Abrahams
problem_details: Government hiring processes for technical and innovation roles in infrastructure and transit are opaque and slow, systematically excluding people who could do the work but do not know the process.

name: Allegheny County DHS
organization: Allegheny County Department of Human Services
problem_details: Local government human services data -- child welfare, behavioral health, housing, criminal justice -- is siloed across agencies and levels of government. Allegheny County has built the most integrated cross-system data infrastructure in US local government and publishes it openly, inviting research partners. Latest report: Using Large Language Models to Strengthen Local Government and Human Services.

name: Alliance of Civic Technologists
problem_details: The civic tech practitioner community has no centralized directory, membership infrastructure, or shared advocacy platform -- making it hard to find collaborators, surface problems, or coordinate responses to policy changes affecting government digital services.

name: Maximum New York
problem_details: No institution in the US systematically trains government employees and technologists in governmental mechanics -- how legislative drafting works, what the budget cycle is, how procurement constrains technology choices. Maximum New York has 180+ students but cannot scale without curriculum partners.

name: BetaNYC
problem_details: NYC's civic tech community lacks a consistent venue for surfacing specific, solvable government data and technology problems and connecting builders with the agencies that have them. BetaNYC runs School of Data, Civic Innovation Fellows, and CityCamp NYC for this purpose.

name: Technologists for the Public Good
problem_details: Civic and public interest technologists lack a national professional home -- a community of practice, career support infrastructure, and shared advocacy platform. TPG runs For the Public conferences across 35 US states and 13 countries and is seeking practitioners in transition and orgs with open problems.

name: Jesse Rothman
problem_details: Criminal justice agencies are deploying AI -- facial recognition, automated report writing, violence prediction, case scheduling -- without the technical capacity to evaluate vendor claims, assess failure risks, or set procurement standards. There is a hunger for reliable guidance but no shared infrastructure to deliver it. The CCJ Task Force released a framework in April 2026 and is explicitly seeking implementation case study partners for 2026.

name: Tricia Brooks
organization: Georgetown University Center for Children and Families
problem_details: States must implement Medicaid work requirements for ~20 million ACA expansion enrollees by January 2027 with no federal guidance (delayed past its December 2025 deadline), no shared technical tools, and compressed timelines. Each state is designing verification, outreach, and renewal systems independently while simultaneously absorbing $911B in federal cuts over 10 years. She is tracking every state's policy decisions and publishing implementation gaps in real time.

name: M. Nolan Gray
problem_details: California passed sweeping zoning and streamlining reforms over the past decade but overall permitting has barely moved and prices keep rising. The remaining blockers are financial feasibility: exorbitant impact fees, unfunded inclusionary mandates, and condominium defect law that make projects that comply with zoning still impossible to finance. He is documenting the specific gap between legal permissibility and financial viability and pushing legislation to close it.
